# Reticle XR (reticlexr) — full documentation

> The complete documentation for reticlexr, the high-level AR SDK for React + Capacitor (WebXR + native ARCore), concatenated for LLM ingestion. Canonical site: https://reticlexr.vercel.app — npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/reticlexr — source: https://github.com/ShahiCrafts/reticlexr



---

<!-- Source: website/content/docs/getting-started.mdx -->

---
title: Getting started
description: Install reticlexr, wire it into a Capacitor app, and place your first model, then test on a real phone over HTTPS.
---

<Info>
This guide will help you get up and running with reticlexr in a few minutes.
</Info>

## Installation

Install the package from npm with your package manager:

<InstallTabs />

The package ships as plain ESM source; there is no build step and no
transpilation. Its renderer/bridge dependencies are **peer
dependencies** your app provides:

| Package | Version (from `package.json`) | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@capacitor/core` | `^8.5.2` | The Capacitor bridge the native facade registers with; any Capacitor 8 app already has it |
| `three` | `^0.180.0` | The WebXR runtime's renderer, scene and GLTF loader |

`react` (`>=16.8.0`) is a peer dependency for the
[`useARCore` hook](/docs/api#usearcore), which lives at
`reticlexr/react`.

<Note>
The package root still re-exports `useARCore` as a **deprecated
alias**, so importing the root entry still pulls React in 1.x.
Framework-agnostic code can import the subpaths instead
(`reticlexr/ar-view`, `reticlexr/web`, `reticlexr/gestures`), which
never touch React.
</Note>

Hand-written TypeScript declarations ship with the package
(`src/*.d.ts`), so TypeScript projects get full checking.

<Step number="01" title="Capacitor setup" id="capacitor-setup">
<div>

For a Capacitor app, install the package and sync:

</div>
<div data-wide>

<Note>
The package's `package.json` carries the
`"capacitor": { "android": { "src": "android" } }` metadata key, so
`cap sync` discovers and registers the Android plugin automatically
(`ARCorePlugin` in the generated `capacitor.plugins.json`, a
`:reticlexr` project in the generated settings). No manual
`settings.gradle` edit is needed; the clean consumer flow is
verified in a scratch Capacitor app.
</Note>

The native Android side, once wired, provides session management, hit
testing and surface events through ARCore. Be aware of what it does
**not** do yet: native model rendering is not implemented: models render
in the WebXR runtime. Read
[WebXR vs native ARCore](/docs/concepts/webxr-vs-native) before planning
an Android-native-only experience.

</div>
<div>

```bash title="Terminal"
npm install reticlexr
npx cap sync
```

</div>
</Step>

<Step number="02" title="Your first AR view" id="your-first-ar-view" stacked>
<div>

The high-level API is `createARView()`. It needs a DOM element to use as
the immersive session's overlay, your buttons and product UI live there.

What happens next is covered by the guides:
[React integration](/docs/guides/react-integration) for component-shaped
usage, [Gestures](/docs/guides/gestures) for tap/pinch/twist, and
[Model preloading & switching](/docs/guides/model-preloading-and-switching)
for product catalogues.

</div>
<div data-wide>

<Note>
`create()` asks the browser for an `immersive-ar` session with the
`hit-test` feature required. `local-floor` is requested when
available, with `local` and `viewer` reference-space fallbacks, so
a device/browser without `local-floor` degrades instead of failing
session creation.
</Note>

</div>
<div>

```js title="first-ar.js"
import { createARView } from 'reticlexr';

const ar = createARView({
  overlay: document.querySelector('#ar-overlay'),
});

// Starts the WebXR session. Defaults shown; every option is optional.
await ar.create({
  showReticle: true,     // centre placement reticle
  showPlaneDots: true,   // dotted visualisation over detected planes
  showShadow: true,      // soft blob shadow under the model
  planeDetection: true,
  lightEstimation: true,
});

// Cache the parsed models so placement and switching are fast.
await ar.preloadModels(['/models/sofa.glb', '/models/chair.glb']);

// Places at the current centre hit test.
const result = await ar.placeModel('/models/sofa.glb');
if (!result.success) {
  // result.code === 'NO_SURFACE' when no surface is in view yet
  console.log('Keep scanning:', result.code);
}
```

```html title="index.html"
<div id="ar-overlay">
  <!-- Buttons here are normal DOM. Mark interactive UI with data-ui so
       the gesture layer ignores it. -->
  <button data-ui onclick="...">Add to cart</button>
</div>
```

</div>
</Step>

<Step number="03" title="HTTPS and phone testing" id="https-and-phone-testing" stacked>
<div>

WebXR immersive AR only runs in a **secure context**: HTTPS, or
`localhost`. A page served over plain HTTP on a LAN address will load, but
session creation will fail: `checkSupport()` reports
`{ supported: false, code: 'INSECURE_CONTEXT' }` in that case, so check
the `code` (and the URL scheme) first when AR refuses to start.

### Zero-setup option

Open this site's [live demo](/demo) on the phone. It is served over HTTPS,
so the only requirements are the device ones below.

### Testing your own app on a phone

Requirements (from the repository's phone-testing guide):

- An ARCore-capable Android phone with Google Play Services for AR
- Current Chrome on the phone
- Phone and development computer on the same Wi-Fi

The example app ships LAN HTTPS tooling with a self-signed development CA:

</div>
<div>

```bash title="Terminal"
cd example
npm install
npm run cert        # generates a private dev CA + server cert for your LAN IP
npm run dev:https   # serves https://<LAN-IP>:5173
```

</div>
<div>

Then:

1. Transfer **only** `example/certs/dev-ca.crt` to the phone, never the
   `.key` file.
2. Install it as a CA certificate (Settings → Security → Encryption &
   credentials; exact wording varies by vendor).
3. Restart Chrome on the phone.
4. Open the printed `https://<LAN-IP>:5173` URL, tap **Start AR**, grant
   camera access, and move the phone slowly over a textured floor or
   table until surface dots appear.

<Tip>
A self-signed certificate without the CA install also works for a quick
look: Chrome will warn once per origin; choose **Advanced → Proceed**.
Pages still count as secure contexts, so WebXR runs, but the warning
returns on every new origin, which is why the CA flow is worth it for
repeated testing.
</Tip>

<Warning>
The generated certificates are development-only and git-ignored. Remove
the development CA from the phone when you finish testing, and never use
these keys in production.
</Warning>

### iOS

iOS Safari does not expose the immersive-ar WebXR flow this SDK's browser
runtime is built on. The WebXR path is an Android Chrome path; plan a
separate implementation for iOS if you need it.

</div>
</Step>


---

<!-- Source: website/content/docs/api.mdx -->

---
title: API reference
description: Every public function, option, type and event in reticlexr 1.1.0, hand-written from the verified source signatures.
---

This reference is hand-written from the source and the shipped
type declarations (`src/*.d.ts`, kept honest against the
implementation by `tsc --checkJs`). Where the JSDoc in the code
disagrees with the implementation, this page documents the
**implementation** and says so.

## Package exports

```js
import ARCore, {
  ARError,
  ARView,
  createARView,
  createARGestureController,
  takeScreenshot,
  enableCustomization,
  addTextures,
  switchModel,
  placeModel,
} from 'reticlexr';
import { useARCore } from 'reticlexr/react';
import { ARCoreWeb } from 'reticlexr/web';
```

| Export | Kind | Layer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ARCore` (default) | Native facade object | Capacitor bridge → Android plugin (web → WebXR engine) |
| `ARView`, `createARView` | Class + factory | High-level facade over the WebXR engine |
| `takeScreenshot`, `enableCustomization`, `addTextures`, `switchModel`, `placeModel`, `moveModel` | Functional helpers (view-first) | Same facade, function style |
| `useARCore` | React hook (import from `reticlexr/react`) | WebXR engine mirrored into React state |
| `ARCoreWeb` | Engine class (import from `reticlexr/web`) | The WebXR runtime itself |
| `createARGestureController` | Factory | Standalone Pointer Events controller |
| `ARError`, `codedError` | Error class + factory | The package's one error convention |

Subpaths: `.`, `./react`, `./web`, `./ar-view`, `./gestures`,
`./package.json`. Deep imports outside the exports map do not
resolve.

<Note>
One identifier everywhere: a placed model is a **`modelId`** on
every layer and runtime. `anchorId` survives as a
**deprecated alias**, the same string, on inputs, results and
event payloads, and is removed in the next major version.
</Note>

## ARCore native facade

The default export. Every method delegates to the Capacitor plugin
registered as `ARCore`, on Android that's the native plugin, on
web it falls through to the WebXR engine (`ARCoreWeb`). Failures
reject with an `ARError` carrying a stable `code` (a runtime code
when one exists, otherwise a per-method `*_FAILED` fallback);
`checkSupport` resolves a result object instead.

```js title="native-facade.js"
import ARCore from 'reticlexr';

const support = await ARCore.checkSupport();
if (support.supported) {
  await ARCore.startSession({ planeDetection: true, lightEstimation: true });
  const hit = await ARCore.hitTest({ x: 0.5, y: 0.5 });
  await ARCore.stopSession();
}
```

| Method | Signature | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `startSession` | `(options?: { planeDetection?, lightEstimation? })` | `Promise<{ success: boolean }>` |
| `stopSession` | `()` | `Promise<void>` |
| `hitTest` | `(options: { x: number, y: number })` (normalised [0, 1]) | `Promise<{ hit, position?, rotation?, planeType?, error? }>` |
| `placeModel` | `(options: { modelPath: string, hitId?: string } \| { modelUrl: string, hitId?: string })` | `Promise<{ modelId: string, anchorId: string }>` |
| `setTransform` | `(options: { modelId, rotation?: {x,y,z} degrees, scale?: number })` | `Promise<void>` |
| `setMaterial` | `(options: { modelId, color: string })` (hex colour) | `Promise<void>` |
| `moveModel` | `(options: { modelId, x: number, y: number })` | `Promise<Object>` |
| `beginDragMove` | `(modelId: string)` | `boolean` |
| `updateDragPoint` | `(x: number, y: number)` (normalised [0, 1]) | `void` |
| `endDragMove` | `()` | `void` |
| `removeModel` | `(options: { modelId })` | `Promise<void>` |
| `getPlacedModels` | `()` | `Promise<Array<{ modelId, modelUrl, position, rotation, scale }>>` |
| `clearModels` | `()` | `Promise<void>` |
| `checkSupport` | `()` | `Promise<{ supported: boolean, reason: string, code?: string }>` |
| `on` | `(eventType: string, callback: (data) => void)` | unsubscribe function `() => void` |
| `addListener` | `(eventType, callback)` | Capacitor listener handle (internal) |

<Warning>
Native-runtime scope (Option B): on Android the session, hit test
and events are real; `checkSupport` returns the actual
`ArCoreApk.checkAvailability()` result and a successful hit test
creates a real ARCore anchor. But the native plugin does **not**
render models: `placeModel`, `moveModel`, `setTransform`,
`setMaterial`, `removeModel`, `getPlacedModels` and `clearModels`
reject with code `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`. WebXR is the runtime that
renders models. See
[WebXR vs native ARCore](/docs/concepts/webxr-vs-native).
</Warning>

### Facade events

`ARCore.on(eventType, callback)` subscribes to the local event bus,
fed by the native event bridge, which installs **lazily on the
first subscription** (importing the package has no listener side
effects):

```js
const off = ARCore.on('modelPlaced', (data) => console.log(data));
off(); // unsubscribe
```

Wired event types: `sessionStarted`, `trackingChanged`,
`surfaceDetected`, `surfaceLost`, `surfaceUpdated`, `sessionStopped`,
`modelPlaced`, `modelRemoved`, `modelTransformed`,
`modelMaterialChanged`, `modelMoved`, `error`. Events are per
runtime; the WebXR engine emits its own set through its listeners
(below), never through `ARCore.on`.

## ARView and createARView

The framework-agnostic facade over one WebXR engine instance. This
is the API the guides and the example use.

```js
import { createARView } from 'reticlexr';

const ar = createARView({ overlay: document.querySelector('#ar-overlay') });
```

Constructor options: `{ engine?, overlay? }`, where `engine` is an
`ARCoreWeb` instance (default: a new one), `overlay` the DOM
element for the immersive session's overlay.

### Session

| Member | Signature / behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `checkSupport()` | → engine `checkSupport()` → `{ supported, reason, code? }` |
| `create(options?)` | Starts the session. Options: `{ overlay?, showReticle = true, showPlaneDots = true, dotSpacing = 0.14, dotSize = 0.014, showShadow = true, planeDetection = true, lightEstimation = true, enableScreenshots = false, framebufferScale = 1 }`. Resolves `{ success, hasOverlay, planeDetection }` |
| `destroy()` | Destroys gestures, then fully disposes the engine (`engine.dispose()`) |
| `onFrame(cb)` / `onPlanes(cb)` | Subscribe to engine frame / plane listeners; both return an unsubscribe function |
| `getSurface()` | Current surface state `{ hasSurface, position, rotation, planeType, confidence }` |
| `getPlanes()` | `[{ orientation, polygon: [{x, y, z}] }]` |
| `setReticleVisible(v)` / `setSurfaceDotsVisible(v)` | Visibility toggles |

```js title="session.js"
await ar.create({ showReticle: true, showPlaneDots: true, dotSpacing: 0.14 });
const off = ar.onPlanes((e) => console.log(e.total, 'planes'));
console.log(ar.getSurface().planeType); // e.g. 'horizontal'
await ar.destroy();
off();
```

### Models

| Member | Signature / behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `preloadModels(urls)` | Loads each URL into the engine cache (`Promise.all`) |
| `placeModel(modelUrl, options?)` | Options: `{ position?, rotation?, x = 0.5, y = 0.5, scale? }`. Hit-tests (centre, or `x, y`) unless `position` is given. Resolves `{ success: true, modelId, … }` or `{ success: false, code: 'NO_SURFACE', reason }` (`reason` is a deprecated alias of `code`). Sets `activeModelId` / `activeModelUrl` |
| `switchModel(modelUrl, options?)` | Options: `{ preserveMaterial = true }`. Keeps placement/transform; falls back to `placeModel` when nothing is placed |
| `moveModel(point?)` | Moves the active model to the surface under a normalised screen point (`{ x = 0.5, y = 0.5 }`). Keeps its scale. Resolves `{ success: false, code: 'NO_SURFACE' }` on a miss; the model stays put |
| `removeModel()` | Removes the active model; no-op if none |
| `getPlacedModels()` | Models placed through this view |
| `clearModels()` | Removes every model placed through this view |
| `setScale(scale)` | Clamped to **[0.1, 5]**, applied uniformly |
| `rotateBy(radians)` | Accumulates `transform.rotationY`, applies a Y rotation |
| `setColor(color)` | Sets the active model's colour (hex string) |
| `addTextures({ name: url })` | Registers named texture URLs; returns `this` |
| `applyTexture(nameOrUrl, options?)` | Options: `{ materialName? }`. Throws if no model is placed |
| `takeScreenshot(options?)` | Delegates to the engine, see [Screenshots](/docs/guides/screenshots) |
| Public fields | `activeModelId`, `activeModelUrl`, `placedModelUrls` (Map), `transform` (`{ scale, rotationY }`), `textures` (a `Map`) |

```js title="models.js"
await ar.preloadModels(['/models/sofa.glb', '/models/chair.glb']);
const placed = await ar.placeModel('/models/sofa.glb');
if (placed.success) {
  ar.setScale(1.25);
  ar.rotateBy(Math.PI / 6);
  await ar.switchModel('/models/chair.glb'); // same anchor, scale, rotation
  await ar.setColor('#222b3c');
  await ar.removeModel();
}
```

### Customization and gestures

`enableCustomization(options?)` wires the gesture controller to
the overlay. It **throws without an overlay**. Options:
`{ modelUrl: string | (() => string), onTap?, onScale?,
onRotate?, onError? }`: `modelUrl` may be a URL string or a
function invoked on every tap; placement errors are delivered to
`onError`. Returns a cleanup function. Full details in
[Gestures](/docs/guides/gestures).

### Functional helpers

The same operations, view-first, for function-style codebases:

```js
import { placeModel, switchModel, addTextures, enableCustomization, takeScreenshot } from 'reticlexr';

await placeModel(ar, '/models/sofa.glb');
await switchModel(ar, '/models/chair.glb', { preserveMaterial: false });
addTextures(ar, { oak: '/textures/oak.jpg' });
const cleanup = enableCustomization(ar, { modelUrl: () => '/models/sofa.glb' });
const shot = await takeScreenshot(ar, { format: 'jpeg', quality: 0.85 });
```

## ARCoreWeb engine

The WebXR engine class behind everything above
(`import { ARCoreWeb } from 'reticlexr/web'`). Advanced consumers
can use it directly; the hook does.

### Configuration

`setConfig(partial)` / `getConfig()`. Defaults:

| Key | Default | Key | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `showReticle` | `true` | `reticleColor` | `0x00ff88` |
| `showPlanes` | `false` | `reticleColorVertical` | `0xff6b6b` |
| `showPlaneDots` | `true` | `planeColorHorizontal` | `0x00ff88` |
| `showShadow` | `true` | `planeColorVertical` | `0xff6b6b` |
| `showBaseRing` | `false` | `shadowOpacity` | `0.4` |
| `dotSize` | `0.02` | `shadowSize` | `1.2` |
| `dotSpacing` | `0.1` | `debug` | `false` |
| `modelCacheLimit` | `20` | | |

<Note>
The facade's `create()` overrides some of these per view (dots at
spacing `0.14`, size `0.014`). Engine defaults apply when you drive
the engine directly. `debug` gates the engine's diagnostic
logging; `modelCacheLimit` caps the GLTF cache (LRU; entries with
live placements are never evicted).
</Note>

### Session and accessors

`checkSupport()`, `startSession({ planeDetection = true,
lightEstimation = true, enableScreenshots = false, framebufferScale = 1,
domOverlay = null })`, `stopSession()`, `dispose()` (full
teardown; the instance can start again), `clearModelCache()`,
`getSession()`, `getRenderer()`, `getScene()`, `getCamera()`,
`getAnchors()`.

### Models

| Method | Signature / behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `loadModel(url)` | Loads (or returns the cache entry) and resolves a fresh `gltf.scene.clone()` |
| `placeModel({ modelUrl, position?, rotation?, scale? })` | Resolves `{ modelId, anchorId }` (`anchorId` = deprecated alias). Inputs are normalised: position `[x,y,z]` or `{x,y,z}`; rotation quaternion or Euler radians; scale number/array/object, clamped to [0.1, 5] per axis |
| `removeModel({ modelId })` | Removes the model; disposal follows the ownership rule |
| `getPlacedModels()` | `[{ modelId, modelUrl, position, rotation, scale }]` |
| `clearModels()` | Removes every placed model |
| `transformModel({ modelId, position?, rotation?, scale? })` | Applies a model transform |
| `switchModel({ modelId, modelUrl, preserveMaterial = true })` | Swaps the model on an existing placement; material carry-over matches by name, then order |
| `setModelColor({ modelId, color })` | Recolours |
| `setModelMaterial({ modelId, metalness?, roughness?, opacity? })` | PBR property update |
| `setModelTexture({ modelId, textureUrl, materialName? })` | Applies a texture |
| `setTransform(options)` / `setMaterial(options)` / `moveModel(options)` | Facade-compatibility shims accepting `modelId` (or its `anchorId` alias); a plain `{x,y,z}` rotation in `setTransform` is Euler **degrees** |

```js title="engine-models.js"
const { modelId } = await engine.placeModel({
  modelUrl: '/models/sofa.glb',
  position: [0, 0, -1.5],
  rotation: [0, 0, 0, 1], // quaternion
  scale: [1, 1, 1],
});
await engine.setModelMaterial({ modelId, roughness: 0.8 });
await engine.removeModel({ modelId });
```

### Queries, events and visualisation

| Method | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `hitTest({ x, y })` | Resolves `{ hit, position?, rotation?, planeType?, code? }`. Centre coordinates use the reticle path; non-centre coordinates perform a ray-based hit test |
| `hitTestAtPoint(x, y)` | The ray-based hit test directly |
| `getSurfaceState()` / `getSurfaceDetectionState()` | Current surface state |
| `getDetectedPlanes()` | Detected plane list |
| `addFrameListener(cb)` / `addPlaneListener(cb)` | Subscribe; return unsubscribe |
| `setReticleVisible(v)` | Toggle the reticle |
| `setPlaneVisualization(v)` / `isPlaneVisualizationEnabled()` | Plane mesh visualisation |
| `setShadowVisible(modelId, v)` | Per-model shadow toggle |
| `setShadowConfig({ enabled?, opacity?, size? })` / `getShadowConfig()` | Shadow tuning |

Frame listeners receive engine events: `surfaceDetected`,
`surfaceLost`, `modelPlaced`, `modelRemoved`, `modelTransformed`,
`modelColorChanged`, `modelSwitched`, `sessionEnded`: payloads
carry `modelId` (with `anchorId` as its deprecated alias). Plane
listeners receive `planeAdded` and `planesUpdated` with payload
`{ type, total, horizontal, vertical }`: counts as **numbers**.

### Screenshots

`takeScreenshot({ format = 'png', quality = 0.92, width?,
height?, includeReticle? })` resolves `{ success, dataUrl, width,
height, timestamp, includesCamera }` or `{ success: false, code?,
error }`. Including the camera feed needs the session started
with `enableScreenshots: true`, see
[Screenshots](/docs/guides/screenshots).

## useARCore

React hook over the WebXR engine, imported from
**`reticlexr/react`**. By default all consumers share one
lazily-constructed engine; pass `{ engine }` (a dedicated
`ARCoreWeb` from `reticlexr/web`) for an isolated, per-instance
hook. It checks support on mount and mirrors engine events into
state.

**State:** `isSupported: boolean | null`, `isSessionActive:
boolean`, `placedModels: Array<{ modelId, modelUrl, position,
rotation, scale }>`, `error: string | null`, `detectedPlanes:
{ horizontal, vertical, total }`, `surfaceState:
{ hasSurface, position, rotation, planeType, confidence }`.

**Methods** (all memoised): `startSession(options)` →
`Promise<boolean>` (options pass straight to the engine, e.g.
`{ domOverlay }`), `stopSession()`, `hitTest(x, y)` (normalised
[0, 1], origin top-left, not pixels),
`placeModel(modelUrl, position, rotation, scale)`,
`removeModel(modelId)`, `getPlacedModels()`, `clearModels()`,
`transformModel(modelId, transforms)`,
`setModelColor(modelId, color)`,
`setModelMaterial(modelId, properties)`, `setConfig` /
`getConfig`, `setShadowConfig` / `getShadowConfig`,
`setShadowVisible(modelId, v)`, `getDetectedPlanes()`,
`setReticleVisible(v)`, `setPlaneVisualization(v)`,
`clearError()`, `getRenderer` / `getScene` / `getCamera`,
`takeScreenshot(options)`.

```jsx title="hook.jsx"
import { useARCore } from 'reticlexr/react';

const ar = useARCore();

await ar.startSession({ domOverlay: overlayElement });
await ar.placeModel('/models/sofa.glb', [0, 0, -1.5], [0, 0, 0, 1], [1, 1, 1]);
// Placed models (with their modelIds) are mirrored into state:
const first = ar.placedModels[0];
if (first) ar.setModelColor(first.modelId, '#a55f3b');
```

<Note>
Transform arguments are **normalised**: positions accept
`[x, y, z]` or `{x, y, z}`, rotations a quaternion array/object or
Euler radians, scales a number, array or object. (In 1.0.0,
`{x, y, z}` objects produced `NaN` transforms, fixed in 1.1.0.) With the shared default engine, one consumer
stopping the session stops it for all consumers; mount the hook
once, or pass a dedicated engine per view.
</Note>

## Gesture controller

```js
import { createARGestureController } from 'reticlexr';

const gestures = createARGestureController({
  element,                  // required: throws if missing
  onTap, onDrag, onPinch, onRotate,
  tapMaxDuration = 260,     // ms
  tapMaxDistance = 12,      // px
  preventDefault = true,
  ignoreSelector = '[data-ui]',
});
gestures.destroy();
```

Payloads: `onTap({ x, y })`, `onDrag({ dx, dy, x, y })`,
`onPinch({ factor, center })` with an **incremental** factor,
`onRotate({ delta, center })` with an incremental delta in
radians. Full guide: [Gestures](/docs/guides/gestures).

## Error conventions

One convention across the package: async methods reject
with an **`ARError`**, an `Error` with a stable, machine-readable
`code`. Result-object APIs resolve with the same `code` on their
failure results. Messages may change; codes are the contract.

| Layer | Convention |
| --- | --- |
| `ARCore` facade | Rejects with `ARError` (runtime code preserved; per-method `*_FAILED` fallback); `checkSupport` resolves `{ supported: false, reason, code }` |
| Engine `hitTest` | Resolves `{ hit: false, code, error }` |
| `ARView.placeModel` | Resolves `{ success: false, code, reason }` (`reason` = deprecated alias of `code`) |
| `useARCore` | Sets `error` state; failure results carry `code` |
| Screenshots | Resolve `{ success: false, code, error }` |

Engine codes include `SESSION_START_FAILED`,
`SESSION_NOT_ACTIVE`, `SESSION_ENDED`, `HIT_TEST_FAILED`,
`HIT_TEST_TIMEOUT`, `HIT_TEST_UNAVAILABLE`, `NO_VIEWER_POSE`,
`MODEL_NOT_FOUND`, `MODEL_URL_REQUIRED`, `MODEL_LOAD_FAILED`,
`NO_SURFACE`, `NO_ACTIVE_MODEL`, `OVERLAY_REQUIRED`,
`CAMERA_CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE`, `CAPTURE_BUSY`, `INSECURE_CONTEXT`,
plus native codes surfaced unchanged (e.g. `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`,
`ACTIVITY_UNAVAILABLE`).

## Model and texture URLs

Model and texture URLs are loaded **as given** (three.js
`GLTFLoader` / `TextureLoader`); the package performs no
validation or allow-listing. Only load models and textures from
sources you control or trust; a GLB is parsed in your page's
origin, so an untrusted file is untrusted content. Cross-origin
URLs need CORS (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, over HTTPS) or
the load fails; same-origin or bundled assets avoid the issue.

## Deprecated aliases

All aliases keep working throughout 1.x and are removed in the
next major version.

| Deprecated | Replacement |
| --- | --- |
| `anchorId` (inputs, results, event payloads) | `modelId`, the same string |
| `modelPath` (engine `placeModel` option) | `modelUrl` |
| `reason` (ARView place result) | `code`, the same string |
| `useARCore` from the package root | `useARCore` from `reticlexr/react` |


---

<!-- Source: website/content/docs/compatibility.mdx -->

---
title: Compatibility
description: What the code requires, and the devices and browsers it has actually been run on.
---

The tables below separate **code-level requirements** (verified by
reading the source) from **tested support** (real device runs,
recorded in [Devices](#devices)). Do not read a requirement as a
support promise: a feature is only "tested" once it has been run on
a recorded device.

## WebXR runtime (browser)

| Requirement | Source | Tested |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Secure context (HTTPS or `localhost`) | WebXR platform rule; `checkSupport()` reports it with a distinct `INSECURE_CONTEXT` code | — |
| `immersive-ar` session support | `navigator.xr.requestSession('immersive-ar', …)` | Chrome 157 · Android 12 ✓ |
| `hit-test` feature | Required feature at session creation | Chrome 157 · Android 12 ✓ |
| `local-floor` feature | Requested first at session creation; falls back to `local`, then `viewer` when unavailable | — |
| `plane-detection` | Optional feature; dots/meshes appear when granted | Chrome 157 · Android 12 ✓ |
| `light-estimation` | Optional; requested when light estimation is on | — |
| `camera-access` | Optional; requested **only** when the session starts with `enableScreenshots: true` (for screenshots, not implied by light estimation) | See the device notes |
| `dom-overlay` | Optional; requested when an overlay element is provided | Chrome 157 · Android 12 ✓ |

The documented test path is **Chrome on an ARCore-capable Android phone**
(see [Phone testing](/docs/getting-started#https-and-phone-testing)).
Chrome versions tested so far: **157.0.8103.78** on Android 12. No
minimum Chrome version is established: only versions actually run
are listed.

iOS Safari does not expose the immersive-ar WebXR flow. The browser
runtime is not an iOS path.

## Native Android runtime (Capacitor)

| Item | Value | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Minimum Android SDK | 24 | `minSdk` default in `android/build.gradle` (overridable by the host project) |
| Compile / target SDK | 36 / 36 | Defaults, overridable |
| ARCore library | `com.google.ar:core` 1.40.0 | Device must be ARCore-capable with Google Play Services for AR |
| Filament | 1.52.0 | Camera-background rendering |
| Java | 21 | Source/target compatibility |

The native Capacitor runtime has not been device-tested yet. The
WebXR runtime has, see [Devices](#devices).

<Note>
The library's Android manifest declares the AR feature (and the
plain camera feature) as `required="false"`, which merges into
your app: host apps stay installable on non-AR devices. Making
AR required is an opt-in from your own manifest, see the
[installation guide](https://github.com/ShahiCrafts/reticlexr/blob/main/docs/INSTALLATION.md).
</Note>

## Frameworks and tooling

| Item | Requirement | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| React | `>=16.8.0` (peer) | Only the hook needs it (import it from `reticlexr/react`). The root entry still re-exports it as a deprecated alias, so root imports still pull React in 1.x |
| `@capacitor/core` | `^8.5.2` (peer) | Provided by the host Capacitor app |
| `three` | `^0.180.0` (peer) | Provided by the host app, one shared copy; duplicates break GLTF class identity |
| Module format | ESM (`type: module`) with an `exports` map | Subpaths: `.`, `./react`, `./web`, `./ar-view`, `./gestures`, `./package.json` |
| TypeScript | Hand-written declarations ship (`src/*.d.ts`) | JSDoc in the implementation is type-checked by `npm run check-types` (`tsc --checkJs`) |

## Devices

| Device | OS | Browser | Date | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Redmi Note 9S | Android 12 | Chrome 157.0.8103.78 | 2026-11-17 | WebXR demo run, see notes below |
| Samsung Galaxy A24 (SM-A245F) | Android 16 | Chrome 157.0.8103.50 | 2026-11-17 | WebXR demo run, tap-to-place confirmed |

Follow-up the same day: when the demo moved to tap-only placement,
tap-to-place failed on the Redmi: the per-tap hit test gave up on
its first (still empty) results frame, so taps missed silently.
Fixed in the library (the point hit test now tolerates a short
grace of empty frames and falls back to the reticle hit, and a
missed tap now surfaces an on-screen hint), and confirmed working
on both devices above.

Notes from the Redmi Note 9S run (the library's first recorded device
test, against the live demo):

- Session start, surface detection, tap-to-place and in-place model
  switching all worked; switching was smooth.
- Pinch-to-scale and twist-to-rotate worked but were jittery and
  hard to control. Root causes found in the gesture pipeline the
  same day, no `touch-action: none` on the overlay, unsmoothed
  digitizer samples, and transform state committed only after an
  async engine call, and fixed in the library source. A confirming
  re-test is pending.
- Screenshots failed with `CAMERA_CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE`: the demo
  did not start its session with `enableScreenshots: true`, so
  camera access was never requested (WebXR can only grant it at
  session start). The demo now opts in; a confirming re-test is
  pending.

If you run the demo on your phone, reporting the device model,
Android version and Chrome version (in a GitHub issue) directly
extends this table.

<!-- Source: website/content/docs/known-issues.mdx -->

---
title: Known issues & roadmap
description: What the v1.0.0 audit found, what 1.1.0 fixed, and what is still open, in plain language.
---

This page summarises a full code audit of v1.0.0 (68 rated findings
with file and line references) and
the 1.1.0 remediation that followed it. Most findings are fixed;
what remains is listed plainly below, including the items that are
open **by decision** rather than by oversight.

## Fixed in 1.1.0

### WebXR engine

- **Hit testing takes coordinates.** `hitTest({x, y})` with
  non-centre coordinates now performs a real ray-based hit test
  (centre still uses the reticle path).
- **Removed models are disposed.** A documented ownership rule
  governs disposal on remove/switch/stop paths; the model cache is
  LRU-capped (`config.modelCacheLimit`, default 20), and
  `engine.dispose()` performs a full teardown (ARView's `destroy()`
  calls it).
- **Plane dots are one `InstancedMesh` per plane** instead of one
  mesh per dot, and surface notifications fire on change at ≤10 Hz
  instead of per frame.
- **The reticle setting is honoured**, `showReticle: false` is no
  longer forced back on at session start, placement or removal.
- **Session-start failures clean up** (no leaked live session), and
  the fallback hit test always settles, including on session end.
- **Reference-space fallback:** `local-floor` → `local` → `viewer`
  instead of `local-floor` or nothing.

### Facade, hook and API shape

- **One model identifier:** `modelId` everywhere (`anchorId` is a
  deprecated alias), and transform inputs are normalised at the
  engine boundary, `{x, y, z}` objects no longer produce `NaN`
  transforms.
- **Hook plane counts work** (the engine's numeric counts are read
  as numbers).
- **`switchModel` material carry-over matches by material name,
  then order**, multi-material models no longer flatten.
- **Enumeration exists:** `getPlacedModels()` / `clearModels()` on
  the engine, `ARView`, the facade and the hook.
- **Per-instance hook engine:** `useARCore({ engine })` isolates a
  view; the default shared engine is constructed lazily.
- **One coded-error convention:** public failures carry a stable
  `code` (`ARError`); messages are unchanged.
- **React is only needed by the hook,** which lives at
  `reticlexr/react`; the native event bridge installs lazily on
  first subscription instead of at import. (The root entry still
  re-exports the hook as a deprecated alias, so root imports still
  pull React in 1.x.)

### Native Android

- **Lifecycle is wired:** pause/resume/destroy are forwarded; the
  render loop restarts reliably for a second session; plugin
  destroy stops and joins the render thread and destroys Filament
  resources in dependency order; the Filament engine is created
  lazily.
- **`checkSupport` asks ARCore** (`ArCoreApk.checkAvailability()`)
  instead of always saying yes, and session creation receives the
  foreground Activity.
- **Anchors are real:** hit tests are served by the render loop
  (the sole `Session.update()` caller) and a successful hit creates
  a real ARCore anchor whose id is returned.
- **The availability retry is bounded** (25 attempts ≈ 5 s, then a
  coded timeout) and can never create a session after stop.
- **The library manifest no longer forces AR-required** onto host
  apps (`required="false"` for the AR and camera features;
  AR-required is a documented opt-in).

### Packaging and docs

- The **`capacitor` metadata key** ships, and the clean consumer
  flow (`npm install reticlexr` → `npx cap sync` → plugin
  registered) is verified in a scratch Capacitor app.
- **Hand-written TypeScript declarations** ship and are kept
  honest by `tsc --checkJs`; the package declares ESM + an
  `exports` map with subpaths; `three` and `@capacitor/core` are
  peer dependencies; lockfiles are committed and the CI workflow
  installs with `npm ci`.
- **Tests exist:** the Vitest suite (27 files, 28 tests) passes
  locally, and the committed CI workflow defines jobs for it
  alongside the type-check, the example build and a Gradle
  `:reticlexr:assembleDebug` build. The workflow has not yet had a
  completed run, so treat the suite as a local verification for now.

## Still open

- **Native model rendering:** scoped out by decision (Option B).
  The native plugin provides session management, hit testing and
  events; `placeModel`, `moveModel`, `setTransform`, `setMaterial`,
  `removeModel`, `getPlacedModels` and `clearModels` reject with
  `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` on native instead of pretending to work.
  Models render in the WebXR runtime. Implementing native
  rendering (Option A) remains an owner decision.
- **Compatibility coverage is one device deep.** The WebXR runtime
  has a first recorded device test (Redmi Note 9S, Android 12,
  Chrome 157, see [Compatibility](/docs/compatibility)); the
  native Capacitor runtime has not been device-tested yet.
- **`npm audit` has never been run.** The audit environment's
  registry proxy refuses the audit endpoint (403), so no
  vulnerability counts exist. The CI workflow defines the audit as a
  non-blocking step; run `npm audit` at the repository root and in
  `example/` wherever the registry permits.
- **SSR:** all entry points pass DOM-less import checks (no
  `window`/`document` access at import; the hook renders to string),
  but a full framework prerender (e.g. Next.js) has not been
  exercised, still TODO.

Still unverified anywhere: `npm audit` results and a full framework
SSR prerender. Both are stated as such at their point of use on this
site rather than asserted.


---

<!-- Source: website/content/docs/changelog.mdx -->

---
title: Changelog
description: Release history for reticlexr, from the repository CHANGELOG, with one claim corrected against the audited code.
---

All notable changes to this project are documented here. The project
follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## 1.1.0 — Unreleased

The audit-remediation release. Summary: the full entry is in the
repository `CHANGELOG.md`.

### Package rename

- The package was renamed from `capacitor-arcore` to **reticlexr**
  before its first publish. `capacitor-arcore` was never published
  to npm; there is nothing to migrate from the registry.

### Behavior changes

- **Native Android is scoped to session + hit-testing (Option B).**
  `placeModel`, `moveModel`, `setTransform`, `setMaterial`,
  `removeModel`, `getPlacedModels` and `clearModels` reject with
  `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` on native; models render via WebXR. Native
  lifecycle (pause/resume/destroy) is wired, `checkSupport` returns
  real ARCore availability, and hit tests create real anchors.
- **The library manifest no longer forces AR-required:**
  `android.hardware.camera.ar` and `android.hardware.camera` are
  `required="false"`; AR-required is a documented opt-in.
- **Screenshots are opt-in:** `enableScreenshots: true` at session
  start; `lightEstimation` no longer implies `camera-access`.
- **One model identifier** (`modelId`) and **one coded-error
  convention** (`ARError`) across all layers.
- The native event bridge installs lazily; the package declares
  ESM + an exports map; `three` and `@capacitor/core` are peer
  dependencies.

### Added

- Drag-to-move: with a model placed, one finger drags it across
  surfaces; the engine re-aims a hit test at the finger every
  frame, so the model stays under it.
- ARView debug readout: `enableCustomization` accepts `debug`
  and `onDebug`. Entries report each tap's pixel and normalised
  point, the hit coordinate, the model's measured base centre,
  and where its centre lies after the tap, so placement accuracy
  can be verified on a phone. The live demo shows them in an
  on-screen panel during AR.
- `framebufferScale` session option: scales the XR render target
  (0.85 ≈ 28% fewer fragments). The live demo runs at 0.85.

- `reticlexr/react` subpath for `useARCore`, plus a per-instance
  `useARCore({ engine })` option.
- `getPlacedModels()` / `clearModels()` on the engine, `ARView`,
  the facade and the hook.
- Hand-written TypeScript declarations; a Vitest suite; committed
  lockfiles; a CI workflow (type-check, tests, example build,
  Gradle assemble).

### Fixed
- Tap and drag accuracy: tap-to-place, tap-to-move and drag
  coordinates are now normalised against the overlay element's
  own bounding rect instead of the window size, so any
  difference between the two (insets, embedding, a resized
  overlay root) no longer displaces the model from the touched
  point. A new end-to-end harness verifies the whole chain
  against an analytic floor: taps land within 0.0001 m of the
  predicted point and project back to the tapped pixel within
  half a pixel.
- Overlapping plane dots: when the same surface is reported as
  overlapping planes, their dot fields no longer overlap. All
  planes' dots are rebuilt in one pass over a shared occupancy
  grid (largest plane first), so each surface shows a single
  clean dot grid.
- Placement centre hardening: the base centre is measured from
  the model's main mesh cluster, so detached stray geometry in
  a GLB (a leftover mesh sitting away from the body) can no
  longer drag the measured centre, and with it the tap point,
  off the model. The footprint used for shadows and base rings
  is measured the same way.

- The audit's BUG / LEAK / PERF / NAT / COMPAT findings: transform
  normalisation (no more `NaN` placements), hook plane counts,
  ray-based hit testing, disposal under an ownership rule with an
  LRU model cache, `InstancedMesh` plane dots, the reference-space
  fallback chain, a bounded native availability retry, and more.
- Tap-to-move (device report, 2026-11-17): a placed model could
  never be relocated, because the gesture layer only placed.
  `ARView.moveModel({ x, y })` is new, and the tap gesture now moves
  the active model to the tapped surface point.
- The live demo no longer carries one model's texture onto the
  next: it switches models with `{ preserveMaterial: false }`, so
  each model keeps its own authored look.
- Rendering economy: the plane dot grid is capped at 2,048 dots
  per plane, animation mixers skip hidden models, and skinned
  meshes opt out of frustum culling in placement clones.

- Drag tracking rebuilt (device report, 2026-11-17): the first
  drag ran one promise-based hit test per pointer move, serialised
  behind a queue, so the model trailed the finger and landed where
  it had been. The engine now tracks the drag inside its render
  loop (`beginDragMove` / `updateDragPoint` / `endDragMove`), and
  one final move lands the model exactly on the release point.
- Placement is by base centre: models whose files carry their
  geometry offset from the origin (the demo astronaut sits about
  0.92 m from its origin and 0.28 m below it) now land on the
  tapped point and stand on the surface, instead of appearing
  displaced and sunk.

### Deprecated

- `anchorId` → `modelId`; engine `modelPath` → `modelUrl`; ARView
  result `reason` → `code`; `useARCore` from the package root →
  `reticlexr/react`. All keep working throughout 1.x.

## 1.0.0 — 2026-09-25

### Added

- High-level `createARView()` abstraction.
- WebXR and Android ARCore integration layers.
- Surface detection, dotted plane feedback, and placement reticle.
- Tap-to-place, pinch-to-scale, and two-finger rotation gestures.
- GLB/GLTF loading, model preloading, and in-place model switching.
- Runtime material, color, and texture customization.
- AR screenshot API and React DOM overlay support.
- React/Vite example application with LAN HTTPS development tooling.

<Note title="Correction: read the parity claim carefully">
The original 1.0.0 entry lists "WebXR and Android ARCore integration
layers" side by side, which readers reasonably took as feature parity.
The v1.0.0 audit verified that the Android layer provides session
management, hit testing and surface events, but **does not render
models**, model rendering, styling and screenshots are WebXR-runtime
features. This note is the correction; the entry above is otherwise
reproduced as published. See
[WebXR vs native ARCore](/docs/concepts/webxr-vs-native) for the
verified split.
</Note>

<!-- Source: website/content/docs/contributing.mdx -->

---
title: Contributing
description: "How to contribute to reticlexr: development setup, what to run before a PR, and the project's versioning rules."
---

Thanks for contributing to reticlexr.

## Development

1. Fork the repository and create a focused branch from `main`.
2. Install the SDK dependencies with `npm install`.
3. Install the example app dependencies with `cd example && npm install`.
4. Run the example with `npm run dev:https` when testing WebXR on a
   physical device.
5. Keep AR/WebXR/Three.js implementation details inside the SDK; the
   example app should consume the public API.
6. Run the available validation/build commands before opening a pull
   request.

## Repository layout

| Area | Path |
| --- | --- |
| JavaScript API (facade, WebXR engine, hook, gestures) | `src/` |
| Native Android plugin | `android/` |
| Example app | `example/` |
| Documentation site (this site) | `website/` |
| Markdown docs (API reference, installation) | `docs/` |

## Before you open a PR

Run the checks locally:

- `npm test`, the Vitest suite (24 files, 25 tests).
- `npm run check-types`, `tsc --checkJs` over the implementation
  and its hand-written declarations.
- `cd example && npm install && npm run build`, the example app
  build.

## What CI checks

The committed workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) defines two
jobs: a `js` job (install with `npm ci`, the type-check, the test
suite, a consumer smoke test, a non-blocking `npm audit`, and the
example build) and a `gradle-assemble` job (`cap sync` plus
`:reticlexr:assembleDebug`). The workflow has not yet had a
completed run, so the local checks above are the verification that
counts. For AR-specific changes, your PR description carries the
rest: include the device/browser details, what you ran, and what
you saw.

## Pull requests

Keep changes focused, describe user-visible behaviour, document public
API changes, and include device/browser details for AR-specific fixes.

## Versioning

This project follows Semantic Versioning. Breaking public API changes
require a major version increment.

title: Architecture
description: "Two independent AR runtimes behind three JS API layers: the module map, the public surface, and both data flows."

The package is a Capacitor plugin with **two independent AR runtimes**
behind **three JS API layers**. There is no build step: the published
entry is the raw ESM source, with hand-written TypeScript declarations
(`src/*.d.ts`) alongside it.

  <line x1="570" y1="158" x2="570" y2="201" stroke="#8b7ff5" strokeWidth="1.6" markerEnd="url(#arr)" />
  <line x1="190" y1="255" x2="190" y2="301" stroke="#8b7ff5" strokeWidth="1.6" markerEnd="url(#arr)" />
  <line x1="570" y1="255" x2="570" y2="301" stroke="#8b7ff5" strokeWidth="1.6" markerEnd="url(#arr)" />
</svg>

*Diagram: the two runtimes of reticlexr 1.1.0 and the layers above them.*

## The three JS layers

| Layer | Files | Sits on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ARCore` facade: session/hit-test/model methods plus a local event bus (`on()`), bridging native events lazily, on first subscription | `src/index.js` (13.4 KB) | Capacitor plugin named `ARCore` |
| `ARView` / `createARView` + functional helpers: single active model, transform state, texture registry, gesture wiring | `src/ar-view.js` (9.8 KB) | WebXR engine only |
| `useARCore` hook + `createARGestureController` | `src/hooks.js` (27.7 KB), `src/gestures.js` (4.7 KB) | WebXR engine only |

The high-level layers **never call the native plugin**. If you use
`createARView` or the hook, you are on the WebXR runtime everywhere,
including inside a Capacitor app, where the WebView runs the same code.

## Data flow: JS → bridge → native ARCore

```
App JS ─ ARCore.startSession() ─ Capacitor bridge ─► ARCorePlugin (UI thread)
  ├─ camera permission check / request
  └─ ARSessionManager.createSession(planeDetection, lightEstimation)
       ├─ ArCoreApk availability / requestInstall
       ├─ new Session + Config (plane finding, light estimation, auto focus)
       └─ onSessionReady ─► ARRenderer + ARViewManager
            (native view inserted behind the WebView; WebView made transparent)

Render loop (dedicated ARRenderThread):
  Session.update() → tracking → planes → camera matrices
  → camera-texture background → Filament render

Events: managers → AREventEmitter → notifyListeners → Capacitor
  → the facade's lazily installed bridge → ARCore.on() subscribers

Hit test: JS hitTest({x, y}) → plugin → latest frame
  → normalised coords → display pixels → frame.hitTest()
```

## Data flow: JS → Three.js → WebXR

```
App ─ createARView({ overlay }) ─► ARView ─► ARCoreWeb
create() ─► setConfig() + startSession({ domOverlay })
  Three.js setup (once): WebGLRenderer, Scene, PerspectiveCamera (70°),
    lights, GLTFLoader, plane groups, reticle
  navigator.xr.requestSession('immersive-ar', {
    requiredFeatures: ['hit-test'],
    optionalFeatures: ['local-floor'?, 'plane-detection'?,
                       'light-estimation'?,
                       'camera-access'? (only with enableScreenshots),
                       'dom-overlay'? (with overlay)] })
  renderer.xr.setSession(); hit-test source from the viewer space;
  reference space: local-floor → local → viewer fallback chain

Per frame: viewer hit test → reticle pose + surface state
  (frame listeners notified on change, at most 10 Hz)
  every 8th frame: detected planes → dot/mesh visualisation
  anchor map → model + shadow transforms → render

Models: GLTFLoader.load(url) → cache → scene.clone() per placement
  → per-instance cloned materials → blob shadow plane per anchor
Gestures: Pointer Events on the overlay ─► facade callbacks ─► engine transforms
```

## The native side at a glance

Eleven Java classes under `android/src/main/java/com/capacitor/arcore/`:
the plugin facade, a session manager (sole owner of the ARCore
`Session`), a Filament renderer with its own render thread, a surface
manager, a coordinate mapper for hit tests, an event emitter, a view
manager, plus an anchor manager that registers the real anchors
created by hit tests, and a model manager that is currently a
registry only (native model rendering is not implemented). What
that means in practice is the subject of
[WebXR vs native ARCore](/docs/concepts/webxr-vs-native).

## Dependencies (verified from package.json)

| Kind | Package | Version |
| --- | --- | --- |
| peerDependency | `@capacitor/core` | `^8.5.2` |
| peerDependency | `three` | `^0.180.0` |
| peerDependency | `react` | `>=16.8.0` |
| Android | `com.google.ar:core` | `1.40.0` |
| Android | Filament (`filament-android`, `gltfio-android`) | `1.52.0` |
| Android SDK | compile / target / min | 36 / 36 / 24 |

Lockfiles are committed for the package, the example app and this
site (`package-lock.json` in each), so installs are reproducible
with `npm ci`; the ranges above are what the package declares, and
the lockfiles pin what actually resolves.
